findings.finding: The new text says that under a prefix entry the rerun 'still needs its own exact-id entry', and it exempts a cited series that 'has an exact-id entry'. B-3 refuses that entry when the registry is loaded: design section 14, and the README's own rule 'No series id is matched by two patterns (an exact id and a prefix ...)'. Probe 1: the base registry plus an exact EXAMPLE-003/rerun under the prefix EXAMPLE-003/ is SHAPE, both for PR and for CONTRACT. A series id has exactly one slash (SERIES), so a prefix covers every series of its packet id. Three things follow. (1) The rerun's exact-id entry can only use another packet-id part. Probe 1: EXAMPLE-004/rerun loads and counts while EXAMPLE-003/first is voided. (2) The exemption can never apply to a series under a prefix. In a loaded registry, _voided_sibling's first branch returns False only where the prefix set is empty anyway. The exemption takes effect only on a registry that load_registry refuses: probe 1's check_merge on that unloaded registry passes. (3) While one sibling is listed, every series under the prefix counts for nothing, not only the rerun. Probe 1: an unrelated EXAMPLE-003/unrelated-later-pr is NO_HEAD_BOUND_ROUND. No registry rule ends that block: a prefix's chain cannot be retired (the README's reading of 'The latest has no supersededAt'), and deleting the entry would leave the records published under it without a brief. The README states none of this. The vector merge-exact-series-with-a-voided-sibling cites EXAMPLE-001/pr, which no prefix covers, so it does not test the exemption its name suggests; under B-3 no vector could. The behaviour fails closed and the owner gate holds, so the problem is accuracy, not safety. The monitor's ruling uses the same 'its own exact-id registry entry' wording.
findings.requiredChange: Make the VOID bullets agree with B-3. Under a prefix entry, the rerun's exact-id entry must use another packet-id part, because B-3 refuses an exact id beneath the prefix. The clause 'unless the cited series has an exact-id entry' cannot arise for a series under a prefix: drop it, or mark it as inert under B-3, in the README's two places and in the docstring. State that while a sibling is listed, every series under that prefix counts for nothing. Rename or re-describe merge-exact-series-with-a-voided-sibling as the case no prefix covers. Flag this to the monitor with the fix: its ruling assumes an entry that B-3 refuses, and it may not intend a lasting block on a prefix's other series. Any change to B-3 or to the block's scope is the monitor's or the owner's rule, not part of this fix.

questions: Q-RR2-FROZEN: the monitor settled it at rev 4's digest freeze (owner_decisions entry 15), and the fix diff does not touch it. Nothing new to recommend.

Q-RR2-VOID-PREFIX (b): the README states it and check_merge partly enforces it, as ruled. Recommendation: keep it, with RR2C4-1's wording fix. Under B-3, a rerun cannot get an exact-id entry beneath its prefix. In practice (b) therefore means that while a VOID sibling is listed, no other series of that packet id counts, and the rerun moves to another packet-id part. If the monitor does not want that lasting block, the choice is the owner's: relax B-3 for this case, or take option (c).

Option (c), refusing prefix entries for CONTRACT, PACKET and PR series. Recommendation: put it to the owner with RR2C4-1, without waiting for the rule to prove fragile. With B-3 as it stands, (c) is the simplest closure. Every head-bound or contract series would then have an exact id, `voided` would not be needed for them, and recovery would always be a new exact entry. The published registry already registers MET-GOV-002/contract by exact id.

The mechanical part drops a blocked series rather than refusing the whole merge, so a merge with another counting series still passes. This matches how check_merge treats any failing series, and the README says so. Recommendation: keep.
